description: Stack online free: tap to drop the swinging block onto the tower and build it as tall as you can. Perfect drops keep your tower wide — one miss and it's over.
faq: How do I drop a block?
Tap anywhere on the game, click, or press Space, Arrow Down or Enter. Each tap drops the swinging block once.
What happens if the block hangs over the edge?
The overhanging part is sliced off and falls away. The tower keeps only the part that landed, so it gets narrower with every off-centre drop.
A drop that lands almost exactly on top of the block below it, within a few pixels. It snaps into place, keeps the tower at full width, and builds your perfect combo.
Does the block swing faster as I play?
Yes. It starts at about 150 pixels a second and speeds up a little with every block you stack, up to about 380 pixels a second.

lede: The one-tap tower builder, in your browser. A block swings back and forth above your tower, and one tap drops it. Land it squarely and the tower grows taller; land it off-centre and the overhang is sliced away, leaving a narrower tower to build on. Each block changes colour as the tower climbs, the swing gets faster, and one clean miss ends the run. It takes five seconds to learn and one perfect drop to get hooked.

p: Press Start stacking and a block starts swinging left and right above the tower. Tap anywhere, click, or press Space to drop it. If any part of the block lands on the tower, it stays: the part that hangs over the edge is sliced off and falls away, and the tower keeps only the part that landed.

Every block you stack is one point, shown in big numbers at the top of the screen. Miss the tower completely and the run is over: you see how many blocks you stacked, which builder rank that earns, and whether you beat your best tower, which is saved on this device.

sections.h: Perfect drops and the shrinking tower
p: Drop a block almost exactly on top of the one below — within a few pixels — and it snaps into place as a perfect drop. A perfect drop keeps the tower at its full width, and perfect drops in a row build a combo, shown with a golden PERFECT badge. The more perfect drops you chain, the taller your tower can grow.

Any drop that is not perfect trims the tower: the overhang is cut away and every block above it is narrower. A tower that starts 240 pixels wide can end up a sliver, so the real game is not dropping fast, it is dropping straight. The block starts swinging at about 150 pixels a second and speeds up a little with every block you stack, up to about 380 pixels a second.

sections.h: The little game that stacked the charts
p: Stacking blocks is one of the oldest arcade ideas: the fairground version had players timing a moving crane to drop prizes into a pile. The one-tap version most people know came from the mobile game Stack, released by Ketchapp in 2016. It asked for exactly one thing — tap at the right moment — and it became one of the most downloaded games of the year, copied in dozens of versions.

The idea works because the feedback is instant: you see the overhang slice away the moment you mistime a drop, and you see a perfect drop snap into place with a golden flash. The version here is the same idea, free in your browser, with a rainbow tower that climbs the sky as you play.

ol: Watch the block, not the tower. Drop when the swinging block lines up with the one below it, not when it reaches the edge.
Drop a fraction early rather than late: the block is moving fastest in the middle of its swing, and a late tap overshoots further than an early one.
After a trimmed drop, slow down. A narrow tower forgives nothing, so wait for the block to come back to the centre before you drop.
Chase perfect drops, not speed. A perfect drop keeps your tower wide, and a wide tower is worth far more than two hurried blocks.
On a phone, hold the device with both hands and tap with a thumb. The tap is the whole game, so keep your thumb hovering over the screen.

p: For another one-tap classic, flap a little bird through the pipes in [[flappy-bird]]. If you would rather clear a board than build a tower, slide tiles and chase 2048 in [[2048]]. You can find every fast, one-more-go game in [[cat:arcade|arcade games]].
